Title: Rohingya rights group 'president' charged over unregistered organisation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A man claimed trial in the Magistrate's Court here on two charges related to the management of an unregistered organisation.
The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) said Zafar Ahmad Abdul Ghani, who had identified himself as president of the Myanmar Ethnic Rohingya Human Rights Organisation Malaysia (Merhrom), was charged under Sections 42 and 48 of the Societies Act 1966.
"Zafar pleaded not guilty to both charges and claimed trial. The court fixed Oct 30, 2026, for mention of the case," it said in a statement.
Section 42 of the Societies Act outlines criminal offences and penalties involving office-bearers or individuals managing an unlawful society, including an unregistered or banned society, while Section 48 deals with acting on behalf of, representing, or assisting an unlawful society.
The RoS said the charges followed an investigation by its enforcement division into Merhrom's activities on social media, including Zafar's statements and publications.
"Checks found that Merhrom was not registered with the RoS, while Zafar was not an office-bearer of any registered organisation using the name," it said.
The department said it took seriously any activities involving the management, operation or promotion of organisations that did not comply with the law, adding that monitoring and enforcement action would continue to ensure compliance with the Societies Act 1966 and related regulations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTViral: Police chase lorry driving against traffic in Pasir Gudang
Article:
PASIR GUDANG: A police chase involving a lorry driven dangerously and against traffic here went viral on social media.
Several videos circulating online showed the lorry being driven at high speed and entering the opposing lane, forcing other road users to take evasive action.
Several police patrol cars were seen pursuing the lorry and attempting to stop it, but the driver initially managed to evade them.
One video showed the chase stretching for several kilometres before police eventually stopped the lorry at a traffic-light junction.
The footage sparked concern among social media users, who said the lorry's reckless driving could have resulted in a serious accident.
However, police have yet to issue an official statement on the incident, including whether the lorry had been reported stolen and why the driver fled from the police.
It is also unclear whether anyone was injured, whether the driver has been arrested and what offences are being investigated.
The New Straits Times has reached out to the Seri Alam district police headquarters.

Title: RM1mil BSN prize helps retiree build new surau for children in Kedah
Article:
ALOR SETAR: "My only intention is to build a better surau for the comfort of children around Alor Senibong, Langgar, to come and learn the Quran," said Arbaai Mat Ali, 66.
Arbaai, a retired civil servant, is the winner of the Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) Premium Savings Certificate (SSP) Millionaire Draw for August 2026, taking home a RM1 million prize.
The former employee of Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital (HSB) here said she did not expect to become a millionaire after starting to save with SSP more than 20 years ago.
"I started saving with SSP by chance after receiving the Excellent Service Award (APC) in 2006, when one of the prizes was BSN SSP.
"Since then, I have regularly added to my SSP savings according to my means," she said when met.
Earlier, Arbaai and five other BSN SSP winners from Kedah were hosted by BSN acting chief executive Mujibburrahman Abd Rashid at an event held here today.
Arbaai said that after retiring about six years ago, she started Quran classes for children at an old surau near her home.
However, she said the wooden surau was in poor condition, with some parts damaged by termites.
"I often prayed for greater sustenance so I could build a new prayer hall for children to attend Quran classes. That blessing eventually came through BSN SSP.
"Work has begun to level the site and lay the foundation, with help from my son. We are donating the prayer hall as a waqf for the community," she said.
Meanwhile, BSN SSP State Draw winner for August 2026, Hariza Tajuddin, 56, who received a Perodua Myvi, said the prize was the biggest she had ever won.
The retired civil servant, who ended her service as a nurse at Yan Hospital near here in January, said she was still shocked when informed that she had won the SSP prize earlier this month.
"I had just returned from performing umrah when I was told that I had won the car. A friend suddenly congratulated me after seeing my name announced.
"Coincidentally, my old car was badly damaged in an accident last June, so this prize is a replacement for the 'loss' I experienced previously," she said.

Title: 44 rescued after flash flood hits JB kindergarten
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Forty-four people, including 37 children and seven teachers, were evacuated after flash floods hit Tadika & Taska Umiku Sayang in Jalan Muhd Amin.
The Fire and Rescue Department said 10 personnel from the Larkin Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 4.14pm, about 21 minutes after receiving a distress call, and launched a rescue operation using a volunteer boat.
All 44 victims were safely evacuated to the Medan Selera Tepian surau.

Title: Uncovering the true craft of translation
Article:
EVERY year on September 30, the global literary community marks International Translation Day, celebrating the craft of translators who carry stories across borders and grant them second lives in new tongues.
To many, translation appears straightforward: an author writes, a translator replaces the words, and a foreign work arrives neatly bound on our shelves.
Often, our attention remains fixed on the plots and characters within those pages. Yet the journeys behind local translations frequently hold stories every bit as fascinating as the literature itself.
Revisiting established classics is a vibrant part of the Malaysian publishing landscape. National Laureate (Sasterawan Negara) A. Samad Said's masterwork Salina (1961), for instance, has been translated into English three separate times: by Harry Aveling in 1975, Hawa Abdullah in 1991, and Lalita Sinha in 2013.
Naturally, when readers encounter a new translation of a familiar classic, they assume it is a retranslation, a fresh effort to interpret the original text for a contemporary readership.
Yet that assumption is not always accurate. Consider Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's 1943 French masterpiece, Le Petit Prince (The Little Prince). Malaysian readers can choose between two Malay translations: Putera Cilik, translated by Ezzah Mahmud (Peanutzin, 2015), and Putera Kecil, translated by Azzah Abdul Rahman (Biblio Press, 2021).
Because both share the same target language and derive from the same French tale, Putera Kecil seems, at first glance, to be a retranslation.
Beneath the surface, however, an important distinction emerges: neither translator worked directly from the French original.
Instead, both relied on an intermediary language – English – a widespread practice known in Translation Studies as indirect or relay translation.
Crucially, the two translators did not consult the same English version. Ezzah Mahmud translated Putera Cilik from Katherine Woods's 1943 English version, which defined the prince's voice in the Anglophone world for five decades.
Azzah Abdul Rahman, by contrast, worked from Ros and Chloe Schwartz's contemporary 2010 English translation. In translation scholarship, a work is strictly classified as a retranslation only if it shares the immediate source text of its predecessor.
Because Ezzah and Azzah drew from two distinct English renderings, the two Malay editions do not actually share the same immediate parent text.
If the genealogical lineage of a translation can take unexpected paths, the titles chosen for translated books tell an equally captivating story. Titles serve as the front door to a narrative, framing our expectations before we turn the first page.
Take Joseph Conrad's debut novel, Almayer's Folly (1895). Translating Conrad's title is notoriously difficult because he chose a word with an intentional double meaning: first, "folly" as foolish delusion, referring to Kaspar Almayer's doomed obsession with finding mythical gold in the Bornean interior; and second, "folly" as an eccentric architectural structure, referring to Almayer's half-built riverside mansion, mocked by the local community.
Capturing both dimensions in a single Malay word is nearly impossible. When scholar and writer Rustam A. Sani first translated the novel for Oxford University Press in 1967, he titled it Istana Impian ("Palace of Dreams").
Rustam embraced the architectural metaphor: the physical ruins of a dreamer's home standing as a monument to collapsed European vanity.
At that time, OUP editor Asraf Abdul Wahab actively championed the modernisation of the Malay language, and scholars have noted that foregrounding Almayer's decline against resilient local figures resonated powerfully with the anti-colonial, nationalist aspirations of post-independence Malaya.
Nearly 50 years later, in 2016, the novel was translated into Malay a second time by Hamidah Hassan and Morne Hashim for Institut Terjemahan & Buku Malaysia.
Released alongside director U-Wei Haji Saari's cinematic adaptation, Hanyut, this version represents a genuine retranslation: both Rustam in 1967 and the 2016 translators worked directly from Conrad's 1895 English prose.
Yet the 2016 translators chose a radically different title: Kemudi ("Rudder" or "To Steer"). The back-cover blurb of the translation informed readers that Conrad had submitted his manuscript in 1893 under the working title "Kamudi", a reference to his maritime roots.
There was just one twist: "Kamudi" was never the book's title. It was actually Conrad's pseudonym.
Anxious about how British critics would receive an unknown Polish sailor, Jozef Teodor Konrad Korzeniowski submitted his manuscript under the pen name "Kamudi", the Malay word for rudder.
Decades later, that was mistaken for a working title, steering the author's secret alias straight onto the cover of the Malay edition.
These stories remind us that literary translation is far from a neutral, mechanical exchange. Behind every book on the shelf lies a series of human decisions, cultural contexts, and historical quirks.
This International Translation Day, when you next browse a local bookstore, take a moment to look past the cover.
Inspect the copyright page, read the translator's preface, and think about the unexpected journeys that delivered those words into your hands!
* The writer is an Associate Professor in Translation Studies at the School of Humanities, Universiti Sains Malaysia. She can be contacted at athaslina@usm.my.

Title: Myanmar cleaner jailed 16 years for stabbing 80-year-old fruit seller
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Myanmar cleaner was sentenced to 16 years in jail by the High Court today after pleading guilty to causing the death of an 80-year-old fruit seller in a stabbing incident three years ago.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin sentenced Shofi Husson Sofo Rahman, 29, a United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees card holder, after he pleaded guilty to causing the death of Ah Kau @ Yow Chow Chong, not amounting to murder.
The offence took place around 6.30pm at a house in Taman OUG on Sept 26, 2023.
The charge framed under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code carries a maximum jail term of 30 years and a fine upon conviction.
The charge, framed under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code, carries a maximum jail term of 30 years and a fine upon conviction.
The court ordered Shofi to serve his sentence from the date of his arrest on Sept 28, 2023.
Shofi, who worked as a cleaner, appeared calm in the dock when the sentence was delivered.
The court heard that Ah Kau, then 80, had gone to the premises where Shofi lived.
Ah Kau had stored fruits at the house and went there to collect them before selling them outside his own house.
An argument then broke out between Ah Kau and Shofi.
Shofi took a knife and stabbed Ah Kau in the neck and body before fleeing the house.
Forensic pathologist Dr Koo Zhao Peng, who conducted the post-mortem examination, found two stab wounds on the face, two on both sides of the neck, one on the right chest and one on the left arm.
One of the stab wounds to the neck had penetrated the neck muscle and a major artery, causing severe bleeding.
The cause of death was certified as stab wounds to the neck.
Around 7.40pm on the same day, the Brickfields police headquarters received a MERS 999 call from Kuala Lumpur Hospital informing them that a man had been stabbed at the house.
Five minutes later, a patrol team arrived at the scene and found Ah Kau lying face down and covered in blood in front of the house.
Medical officers arrived and pronounced him dead.
City police contingent Crime Scene Investigation officer Assistant Superintendent Mazli Azmy recovered several items from the scene, including the bloodied knife.
Acting on information, arresting officer Superintendent Kumares Raja Retnam led a team from the contingent's Special Investigations and Serious Crimes Unit to raid a house in Brickfields.
The team broke down the door and entered the house, where they found Shofi.
He attempted to flee from a room but a struggle ensued before he was arrested.
Hours later, Shofi led investigators to a house in Seri Kembangan, where he pointed out a rubbish bin containing a bloodied T-shirt and pair of pants.
Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed Ah Kau at the scene before Shofi arrived and approached him.
The footage also showed Shofi discarding the knife before fleeing the house.
Deputy public prosecutor Faridah Nurdinie Bahrum urged the court to impose a deterrent sentence to prevent similar incidents from happening again.
"The victim was aged 80 and yet still working. The scene was where he had stored the fruits.
"He was a father and his death had deeply impacted his family.
"The accused, a foreigner, should abide by the country's rules," she said.
In mitigation, lawyer Datuk C. Vignesh Kumar urged the court to consider his client's guilty plea, which he said had saved judicial time.
"A jail sentence of between 12 and 15 years is appropriate as my client is a first offender. He is supporting his wife and a child.
"Throughout his detention in jail, he has been of good behaviour and has never caused trouble.
"His time in jail has had a deep effect on him and he apologises for his actions," he said

Title: Ex-cop loses final appeal over RM16,000 bribe to close commercial crime case
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A former police corporal lost his final appeal to set aside his conviction and three-year jail sentence for accepting a RM16,000 bribe to help close a commercial crime case.
A three-member Court of Appeal bench led by Datuk Azman Abdullah unanimously dismissed Azrol Khalil's appeal and upheld the decisions of the lower courts. Other members of the bench were Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Nadzarin Wok Nordin.
The accused was also fined RM80,000, in default one year's jail.
Radzi who wrote the judgment, said the court found there was evidence suggesting that Azrol's superior, identified as SP11, may also have been involved in the request for the bribe.
However, the court rejected Azrol's defence that he was merely collecting the money on behalf of SP11.
"The evidence showed that the appellant played a role in asking for the bribe, gave the complainant the assurance that his case would be closed in return for the payment, negotiated the amount from RM20,000 to RM16,000 and met the complainant to receive the money.
"It is unreasonable for the appellant to involve and expose himself to an act of corruption by doing all these things if he himself had no interest whatsoever in the bribe money.
"The evidence showed the appellant's active role in negotiating the amount to be paid by the complainant until the money was received and placed in his shirt," he said.
Azrol, who was then a corporal with the commercial crime investigation division at the Gombak district police headquarters, was charged with accepting RM16,000 from Mohd Azli Abu Bakar on Feb 7, 2022.
The money was an inducement to have a commercial crime case against Mohd Azli, which was being investigated for cheating, closed.
The prosecution's case was that Azrol initially sought RM20,000 before the amount was reduced to RM16,000.
Azrol's defence was that he was merely collecting the money for SP11 and that the money was also meant to be distributed to several others.
He also argued that he did not have the authority to close Mohd Azli's case.
On that point, the Court of Appeal held that Section 16(a)(B) of the MACC Act did not require the person receiving the bribe to be the same public officer who had the power to carry out the promised act.
"An offence may still be committed where the recipient of the bribe and the person with the authority are two different persons, subject to evidence of a nexus between the recipient of the bribe and the person with the authority."
The court also said the prosecution did not have to prove that Mohd Azli's case was actually closed.
"It is sufficient if the act involving the exercise of authority was merely proposed or might take place.
"This means an offence is still committed when a bribe is corruptly received and the matter involving the authority of a public officer is merely promised, proposed or anticipated to take place," the judge said.
The court also found that the appellant failed to rebut the statutory presumption under Section 50(1) of the MACC Act that the money had been received corruptly.

Title: UiTM Holdings RM157mil losses a legacy issue, says Fathul Bari
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The RM157 million in accumulated losses by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd are a legacy issue dating from 2017 to 2021, not new losses under the current management.
Its chairman, Datuk Dr Fathul Bari Mat Jahya, said the new leadership was committed to resolving the issue and would use Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's criticism as a catalyst to accelerate the recovery process.
"The RM157 million figure was reported as early as 2023, and the Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) at the time explained that it was accumulated losses from 2017 to 2021.
"The issue was also examined in the 2022 Auditor-General's Report and the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) proceedings before the report was tabled in 2024.
"These are facts of the chronology and a legacy issue. We are not using this issue as an excuse, but identifying the problems that need to be resolved," he said in a statement.
Datuk Mohd Shukrie Mohd Salleh is currently UiTM Holdings chief executive officer, a position he has held since January 2025, while Fathul Bari was appointed chairman in August 2025.
Fathul Bari said the new leadership should be assessed based on its integrity, implementation and current results in addressing the trust deficit inherited from the previous management.
He also called on all parties not to politicise efforts to revive the university's holding company.
"This is not a political issue, but about restoring an asset belonging to the university. If UiTM Holdings is strengthened, its value will return to UiTM. If it is weak, the university will also bear the consequences," he said.
He also proposed that the prime minister, who is also finance minister, consider a national framework to grant public university companies a First Right of Refusal (FROR).
"FROR is not a free project or a monopoly, but an opportunity to compete first in a professional manner based on merit, due diligence and competitiveness within their respective university ecosystems.
"If university companies are capable of implementing projects competitively, it would be more strategic for the economic value to remain within the ecosystem and for the profits to be channelled back towards strengthening the university," he said.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) had previously investigated allegations of misconduct that resulted in RM157 million in losses by UiTM Holdings.
MACC confirmed that the investigation, which began in 2023, was still ongoing, including examining issues related to a 50-megawatt solar project in Gambang, Pahang.
The MACC investigation is focused on several issues, particularly involving funds and several investments made by UiTM Holdings that resulted in losses amounting to millions of ringgit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration Dept denies Myanmar teen was repatriated
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has denied claims that a female Myanmar teenager was repatriated to her home country yesterday, saying she remains detained at an Immigration Depot.
Its director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said checks confirmed that the teenager was not involved in yesterday's repatriation programme aboard a Myanmar military vessel.
"The department takes note of concerns raised, particularly regarding the safety and welfare of detainees.
"In carrying out its responsibility to enforce immigration laws, the department also gives attention to humanitarian considerations, subject to prevailing laws and procedures," he said in a statement.
Zakaria said the management of immigration detention depots was carried out according to established provisions and international standards, including the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners, also known as the Nelson Mandela Rules.
He added that internal controls were also implemented under the Immigration Regulations (Administration and Management of Immigration Depots) 2003 and the Director-General of Immigration's Standing Orders on the Administration and Management of Immigration Depots, taking into account the principles of humane treatment.
Zakaria urged the public not to disseminate unverified information that could cause confusion over the actions and processes carried out by the department.
Yesterday, 1,476 Myanmar detainees
were sent home
in the first phase of a repatriation programme aboard three Myanmar naval vessels, including a hospital ship.
Home Ministry deputy secretary-general (Policy and Control) Datuk Makhzan Mahyuddin said the group comprised 1,370 men, 79 women, 20 boys, and seven girls aged between eight and 60.
On July 29, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Myanmar had agreed to take back about 5,000 of its citizens held in Malaysia following discussions between the two countries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Republicans pour money into dozens of US House races previously considered 'safe'
Article:
REPUBLICANS are pouring money into more than three dozen US House races previously considered "safe" after internal polling showed they could be vulnerable in the Nov 3 election, according to three Republican operatives familiar with the party's thinking.
The shift is already starting to show in advertising reservations and campaign finance filings.
Since Sept 1, major Republican groups and megadonors have begun spending in at least 39 congressional races where they haven't previously deployed money this cycle, a Reuters review of spending by some of the largest Republican political groups shows.
Many of the candidates receiving new support sit in Republican strongholds and are still running ahead of Democratic opponents in public polls, these people said, indicating rising worry among party leaders over whether voters will use the Nov 3 election to air dissatisfaction over US President Donald Trump's policies.
House Republican leaders recently warned dozens of campaigns that the party's internal data shows that they cannot assume they will win, even if they are currently ahead in public polls and represent districts Trump won by double digits, two of the people said.
"Republicans are playing defence in some of the strongholds that they're used to not having to worry about," said Republican strategist Ron Bonjean, a partner at bipartisan public affairs firm Rokk Solutions.
Republicans currently hold a narrow 218-214 majority in the House, with one independent caucusing with Republicans and two vacancies.
Democrats would need to net at least four seats in the midterms to take control of the chamber next year.
MASSIVE WAR CHEST
Two Republican operatives working with party leaders said they're using their larger spending power to stifle Democrats before they have a chance to attack.
They said the party was taking out "insurance policies" to ensure Republican-held districts remain in the party's hands.
"Republicans are deploying our massive war chest to drive voters to the polls and supercharge our candidates," said Natalie Baldassarre, national press secretary for the Republican National Committee.
"We're not taking anything for granted, because, unlike Democrats, Republicans aren't throwing in the towel on races we can win."
Republican Representative Bryan Steil is one telling example.
His Wisconsin district voted for Trump by about 4.5 percentage points in 2024 and is rated "lean Republican" by Cook Political Report.
Still, conservative super PACs dumped US$1.5 million on his race this month, their first investment of this election cycle. A representative for Steil declined to comment.
In North Carolina's 3rd Congressional District east of Raleigh, Representative Gregory Murphy this month received US$131,107 from a conservative PAC a week ago – the first outside spending on his behalf in the midterms. Democrats have spent over US$326,000 trying to oust him since July.
Trump won the district by 14 percentage points and Cook rates it "solid Republican." Murphy's office didn't return a request for comment.
The emergency deployments reflect a harsh reality: economic strain is battering traditionally Republican strongholds.
Rising gas prices, energy costs and fertiliser expenses are hitting voters in the agricultural heartland particularly hard.
One Republican House campaign aide said the environment for candidates in Iowa, Kansas and other Midwest states was "dire" as diesel prices soar.
"We're in this crucial period in the last 30 days where candidates have to really make a case, given how tough the headwinds are," said Kevin Madden, who advised former Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney and is now senior partner at corporate advisory firm Penta Group.
Campaigns are running as if they are behind in the polls "even in red districts or traditionally safe" ones, Madden said.
OUTSPENDING DEMOCRATS
More than US$1.56 billion, overall, has been spent by independent committees on federal elections so far, with roughly US$496 million deployed just since Labour Day, according to a Reuters analysis of super PAC spending.
That figure doesn't include all spending by dark money nonprofits that do not disclose their donors.
Republicans have reserved at least US$888 million in advertising over the coming weeks, compared to at least US$666 million for Democrats, according to AdImpact, which tracks political advertising.
No Going Back PAC, which is fully funded by Trump's super PAC MAGA Inc., is leading the surge, Federal Election Commission records show.
"That's the advantage of having a shit ton of money," said one Republican operative working on Trump's midterm strategy. "We're not going to let Democrats take free shots on goal."
Over the last three weeks through Frday, Republican-leaning super PACs have outspent Democrats by almost 2-to-1, showering races with roughly US$309.7 million since Labour Day compared with US$174.2 million going to help Democratic candidates, the FEC data shows.
"Republicans have air superiority. House Democrats are scrambling to catch up with the very limited resources they have," said Mike Marinella, national press secretary for the National Republican Congressional Committee, which works to elect Republicans to the House.
Democrats acknowledge their funding disadvantage but say the Republican push to spend money on districts that Trump won easily reflects the trouble the party faces in the midterms.
"Republicans are running scared, know they've lost the American people, and are trying one last hail mary to spend their way out of certain defeat," said Viet Shelton, spokesman for the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee.
In one district in south Texas that Trump won by 18 percentage points in 2024, Republican groups have pumped about US$2 million into text messages, direct mail and digital ads since Sept 5 to help incumbent Representative Monica De La Cruz keep her seat.
Cook Political Report moved her seat from "lean Republican" to "tossup" on Friday.
De La Cruz is grateful for her supporters helping defeat her rival, her campaign manager said, when asked about the money spent by her Republican backers.
* The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rain improves air quality in Johor, but haze persists in Pasir Gudang
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Heavy rain brought relief from the haze in Johor, with air quality improving in several areas, although four monitoring stations remained in the unhealthy category.
The biggest improvement was recorded in Segamat, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) fell from 160 to 90. Tangkak dropped from 165 to 90, while Batu Pahat fell from 167 to 100.
Kluang also recorded an improvement, with its API falling from 155 to 110, but it remained in the unhealthy category.
In southern Johor, however, haze persisted, with Pasir Gudang recording the highest API at 164, followed by Larkin (162), Kota Tinggi (155) and Pengerang (152).
The 4pm readings showed a clear contrast between northern and central Johor, where rain brought improvements, and southern districts, where air quality remained unhealthy.
At the start of the day, all eight Johor monitoring stations recorded unhealthy readings, with Pasir Gudang at 173, Larkin 170, Batu Pahat 167, Tangkak 165, Kota Tinggi 164, Pengerang 163, Segamat 160 and Kluang 155.
The improvement followed rain in parts of Johor, which helped clear the haze.
Malaysia Meteorological Department director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the haze in southern Johor was linked to smoke from Sumatra, carried across the Straits of Malacca by prevailing winds during the Southwest Monsoon.
The regional haze has also affected neighbouring Singapore, with smoke from fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan contributing to deteriorating air quality.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man who attempted to abduct six-year-old linked to 'gila isim', says exco
Article:
MELAKA: A man who attempted to abduct a six-year-old girl in Ayer Molek last night is believed to have been experiencing a condition referred to as 'gila isim'.
Melaka Education, Higher Education and Religious Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Rahmad Mariman said the man, from Sungai Petai, Alor Gajah, was also believed to have behaved unusually, including snatching a road user's mobile phone on the pretext of wanting to contact police.
"After that, he fled by wading through a river to wash his face before attempting to steal another person's car.
"Members of the public have since detained him following the incident involving the child," he said when contacted.
Rahmad, who is also Ayer Molek assemblyman, said the man was linked to 'gila isim', which he said was associated with claims of deviant teachings.
It was reported that the man had acted aggressively and attempted to abduct the girl.
The incident, which occurred around 8.12pm, was recorded by members of the public before several video clips went viral on social media.
Before the incident, the same man was also linked to two other incidents, including an attempt to steal a vehicle with children inside and allegedly assaulting an elderly person.
A remand application is expected to be made at the Melaka Court Complex in Ayer Keroh today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mara targets RM1bil sales by Bumiputera automotive entrepreneurs next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) is targeting RM1bil or more in sales by Bumiputera automotive entrepreneurs next year through efforts to expand their participation and ownership in the sector.
Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the target was based on the agency's current performance, with 534 automotive entrepreneurs recording sales of more than RM660 million this year.
"Of this number, we have offered more than 2,403 job opportunities. If we can drive this agenda together with our strategic partners, we can achieve that target," he said after officiating the pre-launch of Mara Automotive Ecosystem (Matec) 2026 at Busana Mara here today.
Matec 2026 is scheduled to be held in Bukit Jalil from Nov 27 to 29.
The event is a strategic platform to build connections, create opportunities and strengthen an ecosystem linking entrepreneurs, industry, technical and vocational education and training (TVET), technology, talent, financial institutions, government agencies and the market.
Asyraf said efforts to expand Bumiputera participation and ownership in the automotive sector should go beyond producing skilled workers to developing them into entrepreneurs and business owners.
He said TVET was also among Mara's key focuses in ensuring a continuous supply of trained workers for the automotive sector.
Of Mara's 395 educational institutions nationwide, 270 focus on TVET, while 30 per cent of its TVET institutions specialise in automotive-related fields.
"Of the 222 GiatMara centres, almost all GiatMara branches nationwide have programmes related to automotive," he said.
Asyraf said the training offered ranged from basic skills to high-technology fields such as electric vehicles (EVs), while also allowing students and trainees to pursue higher education, including at Universiti Kuala Lumpur (UniKL) and the German Research Institute.
He said automotive-related fields were among the most popular choices among Bumiputera students.
"Mara cannot operate alone, but must strengthen strategic cooperation with industry partners to expand Bumiputera participation across various segments of the automotive sector.
"We must create synergies and drive strategic cooperation with industry partners who have expertise in specific areas to expand Bumiputera participation across various segments of entrepreneurship, particularly in the motoring and automotive sectors," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas' sustainable fuel Mercedes-AMG F1's edge over other teams – Wolff
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) use of advanced sustainable fuel (ASF) in this season's Formula One is set to be Mercedes-AMG's competitive edge against other teams this year.
Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One team principal and chief executive officer (CEO) Toto Wolff said sustainable fuel is the way forward for the team especially as energy transition is becoming more prominent globally.
"We knew that the sustainable fuel component is going to make the winning difference this year and the work that has been done is literally tremendous.
"Sustainable fuel is the way forward. In Formula One, we are talking about new engine regulations and V8s in the future and a smaller battery or a smaller turbo or ways to reduce the weight.
"The sustainable fuel is out of the question.That's continuing forever," he said at a press conference here today.
Petronas is co-developing 100 per cent ASF for the Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team starting in the 2026 Formula One season.
Petronas executive vice president and CEO Datuk Seri Sazali Hamzah said that the ASF development demonstrates the close collaboration between Mercedes-AMG and Petronas to deliver performance on the track.
"This fuel has been developed by local Malaysian fuel specialists and there are three main players of this development.
"I'm really proud that they are actually from the home ground. The team is so far living at the front of the grid, maintaining a strong position in both the contractor and driver's championship.
"And we see that our involvement in Formula 1 has an opportunity to push the boundary of innovation with supporting a more sustainable fuel," he added.
The race returns to Sepang this year after a nine-year absence. The Formula One Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix will be held from Oct 2 to 4.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] No decision on minimum wage yet, earliest announcement on Budget day
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has yet to decide on the minimum wage revision, with the earliest possible announcement expected when the 2027 Budget is tabled on Oct 9.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, at today's cabinet meeting, had directed that several aspects be studied before any announcement is made.
"The prime minister asked for several aspects to be studied more carefully. If there is an announcement, one likely date is the Budget presentation on Oct 9," he said at a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here.
This comes amid expectations that the government will
announce
a higher minimum wage under the 2027 Budget.
On Saturday, Anwar said the government was dissatisfied with the wage levels despite rising productivity and high profits by some companies.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said stronger measures to address the issue would be among the government's priorities in the upcoming Budget.
Anwar said the government had already taken steps to raise wages, including increasing public sector salaries, raising the private-sector minimum wage to RM1,700 and setting a RM3,100 minimum wage for government-linked investment companies (GLICs).
However, he said these measures were not enough to ensure workers benefited fairly from economic growth and rising productivity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court sets Oct 30 deadline for autopsy report in woman murder case
Article:
BATU PAHAT: The magistrate's court here today gave the prosecution until Oct 30 to obtain the autopsy report of a woman allegedly murdered by her boyfriend in January.
Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno fixed the date after deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim told the court that the post-mortem report was the only outstanding document.
She said the investigating officer had made a second application for the report on Aug 24.
"Previously, two reports — the post-mortem and closed-circuit television (CCTV) recording — had yet to be received.
"However, the prosecution has since received the CCTV report," she said.
Unemployed Lim Chee Seong, 44, is
charged with murdering
his girlfriend, salon worker Lim Bee Lan, 41, at a house in Jalan Damai 2, Taman Damai 11, between 10pm on Jan 26 and 11am the following day.
He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, with whipping of up to 12 strokes if the death penalty is not imposed, upon conviction.
The case came to light after Bee Lan's family was unable to contact her, prompting a search that led police and firefighters to break into the two-storey terrace house.
She was found unconscious inside the house, while Lim was found critically injured beside her after allegedly attempting suicide by slashing his neck and left wrist with a sharp weapon.
Jealousy was among the suspected motives, with Lim believing that the victim was involved with another man.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Singapore test seven SOPs for RTS Link cross-border emergencies
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Malaysia and Singapore have tested their joint response to cross-border incidents involving the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link as both countries step up preparations for its Jan 1 operation.
The RTS Link Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Exercise – Table Top Exercise, held here yesterday, focused on strengthening coordination between agencies from both countries in managing incidents that could disrupt RTS Link operations.
The exercise, organised by the National Security Council in collaboration with Singapore's Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA), also tested and validated seven jointly developed standard operating procedures (SOPs) for managing cross-border incidents.
The joint framework sets out responsibilities when an incident occurs, including when a train completes its journey, stalls in either country's territory or within the 17-metre border stretch.
It also provides for mutual assistance and controlled cross-border deployment of emergency personnel.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad attended the closing ceremony of the exercise.
The exercise provided a platform for Malaysian and Singaporean agencies to test their coordination, communication and response mechanisms in dealing with potential incidents involving the cross-border rail link.
It also reflected efforts by security agencies in both countries to ensure procedures for handling incidents are clearly established and can be activated effectively once the RTS Link begins operations.
The RTS Link, connecting Bukit Chagar in Johor Baru and Woodlands North in Singapore, is expected to increase cross-border connectivity between the two countries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ukraine's war costs for 2026 hit US$155 billion, PM says
Article:
KYIV: Ukraine's total war costs will reach US$155 billion this year, and Kyiv is working to close a US$27 billion funding gap to ensure it can conduct active combat operations at the start of 2027, Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said on Wednesday.
Koretskyi said the government planned to cover US$7 billion of the gap through strict public finance austerity, budget optimisation and cost reallocation, and was in talks with partners on how to cover the remaining US$20 billion.
It is the first time Kyiv has released an estimate of its annual war costs, and there was no comparable figure for 2025.
On Monday, Koretskyi said that Ukraine will postpone some spending commitments, including reconstruction work, because of delays in receiving aid from its foreign backers.
The government will carry out these projects eventually, "but for now, all resources must be directed toward critical areas", Koretskyi said on Telegram, listing defence and social welfare as priorities.
Russia's four-and-a-half-year offensive has battered Ukraine's economy, causing billions of dollars in destruction and punching a huge hole in its neighbour's finances.
The Ukrainian government said earlier this month it would seek an additional US$53 billion in foreign aid next year, including from the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, to make up for the shortfall.
"The situation regarding public finances remains challenging," Koretskyi said.
"Some of the planned international funding has not yet arrived, partly because Ukraine has not managed to fulfil certain commitments made to international partners on time," he added.
"We are deferring non-priority expenditures. This applies to new construction, reconstruction, or major repairs that are not critically important, as well as public realm improvements such as parks, public squares, fountains, or the re-laying of paving stones," he said.
Earlier this month, the Ukrainian government announced it planned to spend a record two thirds of its budget on defence next year as costs mount in the war with Russia.
The Ekonomichna Pravda newspaper reported that the finance ministry had postponed spending on preparing the energy system for winter until December owing to a lack of funds.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zoo Melaka welcomes male black panther cub
Article:
MELAKA: Zoo Melaka is celebrating the arrival of a male black panther cub, which was born naturally on July 22.
The cub weighed 1.09kg at birth and was born to six-year-old female Minah Beting and 11-year-old male Tommy.
Zoo Melaka said the cub was in good health, growing stronger and becoming increasingly active under its mother's close care.
The cub was two months and seven days old as of yesterday.
In a Facebook post yesterday, the zoo invited the public to suggest names for its newest arrival.
The cub's arrival adds to Zoo Melaka's ongoing wildlife breeding efforts and gives visitors an opportunity to follow its growth under its mother's care.
Members of the public can submit their name suggestions through Zoo Melaka's social media platforms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Supermarket awning collapses during heavy rain, damages three motorcycles
Article:
KEPALA BATAS: A supermarket lobby awning collapsed during strong winds and heavy rain, damaging three parked motorcycles.
No injuries were reported.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the incident occurred at Sunshine Supermarket in Jalan Dagangan 2, Pusat Bandar Putra Bertam Perdana, at 1.37pm.
He said initial information indicated that the lobby roof structure collapsed due to strong winds accompanied by heavy rain, hitting three motorcycles parked nearby.
"The motorcycles' owners were not at the location when the incident occurred, and there were no casualties," he said.
John said the operation team cordoned off the affected area and ensured it was safe and inaccessible to members of the public.
"After ensuring the location was safe and there were no other hazards, the site was handed over to the Sunshine Mall management for further action," he said.
The operation ended at 2.48pm, with police also assisting at the scene.
Meanwhile, several areas in Kepala Batas and Bukit Mertajam were inundated by floodwaters.
However, no evacuation was warranted.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Fahmi: Indonesia yet to respond on offer of firefighting assets
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia is still waiting for Indonesia to respond to its offer of assets to help put out fires there, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said
Fahmi said the matter was discussed in the cabinet meeting following Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's visit to Indonesia, where he met President Prabowo Subianto.
"At this point, Wisma Putra has not received a response to the note it sent to the Indonesian side.
"So we are still following official channels and direct discussions between the top leaders," he said at a post-Cabinet meeting press conference.
When asked whether the cabinet had discussed the haze and arrangements if it worsened this weekend, Fahmi said it was not discussed.
He hoped the haze would improve, adding that it sometimes rains.
He said three major events were expected from Oct 2 to 4: Le Tour de Langkawi, the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP in Malaysia 2026 and the Standard Chartered Marathon.
"For the events the government is managing, including F1, the ministry says they will proceed," he said.
Yesterday, Indonesian Ambassador to Malaysia Raden Datuk Mohammad Iman Hascarya Kusumo said the country had
pledged to step up operations
to contain forest and land fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bank Negara imposes penalties on three companies for non-compliance amounting to RM40,400
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia imposed administrative monetary penalties (AMPs) of RM22,000 on Wawasan Ilham (M) Sdn Bhd (WISB) and RM6,900 on SMJ Teratai Sdn Bhd for failing to comply with customer due diligence (CDD) requirements.
Bank Negara said it discovered the breach following an on-site supervisory examination of WISB.
"During the examination, it was found that WISB had failed to conduct CDD on a customer for a money-changing transaction due to inadequate oversight and weak compliance culture," it said in a statement.
The central bank noted that it also discovered the breach following a supervisory examination of SMJ Teratai.
"During the examination, it was found that SMJ Teratai had failed to conduct CDD on a customer for money-changing transactions due to a lack of reasonable care in implementing the CDD requirement by its staff," it said.
Meanwhile, Bank Negara also imposed an AMP of RM11,500 on Ruhanmas Forex Sdn Bhd for failure to comply with targeted financial sanctions requirements.
It said Bank Negara discovered the breaches following an on-site supervisory examination of Ruhanmas.
"During the examination, it was found that Ruhanmas had failed to maintain a sanctions screening mechanism and to conduct sanctions screening on its customers.
"These breaches were attributed to Ruhanmas' lack of understanding of applicable regulatory requirements," it added.
All the companies have paid the penalties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cabinet prays for Dr Mahathir's health as he remains under observation at IJN
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has prayed for the health of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, who is under observation at the National Heart Institute (IJN).
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the cabinet also recorded its condolences to Dr Mahathir and his family following the passing of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali.
"First, the prime minister, the cabinet and the government record their condolences to Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and family on the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, may Allah bless her soul.
"She was a highly respected woman leader and stateswoman," he said at a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here.
MORE TO COME

Title: PH sees room for cooperation ahead of Melaka election
Article:
SHAH ALAM: PH sees room for cooperation with any party or coalition, including BN, in the Melaka election.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said he had met PKR leaders in Melaka yesterday and heard views from PH Melaka.
He said a meeting with BN would be held soon to explore possible areas of cooperation.
"There are strategies that need to be considered if both coalitions work together.
"I need to finalise the matter with the PKR central leadership council so that we can make a policy decision on the next step.
"Either we contest under a common understanding with several parties, or we focus on our respective areas while reaching agreements with certain parties," he told reporters after the launch of the Selangor Road and Highway Strategic Plan 2026-2035 (Jalur Selangor) here today.
Earlier, media reports quoted BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki as confirming that negotiations and discussions on the coalition's direction for the Melaka election were still ongoing.
Asyraf was reported to have said that any developments remained at the negotiation stage among the leadership.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sergeant major in the dock for leaking info on police raids
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A policeman pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to four charges of accepting bribes amounting to RM2,400 four years ago.
Roslee Mamat, 43, a sergeant major with the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division at the Setiu Police headquarters, was charged with accepting bribes ranging from RM400 to RM1,000 from an individual as an inducement to provide advance information on police operations or raids, thereby enabling the individual to take precautionary measures or flee to avoid arrest.
The offences were allegedly committed at a bank branch in Shah Alam, Selangor, and Masjid Gong Terap in Setiu in October and December 2022.
The charges were framed under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, punishable under Section 24(1) of the same act, which carries a maximum prison term of 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the bribe, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
Judge Azman Mustapha set bail at RM6,000 in one surety and fixed Oct 27 for mention.
Roslee was also ordered to surrender his passport and report to the MACC office every month.
MACC deputy public prosecutor Nur Amalina Najwa Mohd Ali prosecuted, while Roslee was represented by lawyer Mohd Fakhrul Fikri Mokhtar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Nepal agrees to expedite status confirmation of 55 untraced Malaysians
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Nepal has agreed to help expedite the process of confirming the status of 55 Malaysians who remain untraced following the disaster in the country, said government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Fahmi said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had spoken to his Nepali counterpart yesterday, Balendra Shah, during which the latter agreed to the request.
"Nepal's prime minister has informed of his agreement to help speed up the process of confirming the status of the 55 Malaysians who remain untraced following the disaster in Nepal," he told reporters at a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here.
Fahmi said Anwar had directed Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar to hold further discussions urgently with the relevant Nepali authorities to expedite the process.
"As it involves legal and court aspects, the attorney-general has been tasked with expediting it," he said.
Wisma Putra said on Sept 14 that the conclusion of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team's
(Smart) deployment in Nepal
did not mean efforts to establish the status of the 55 had ended.
The 55 Malaysians have been
listed as uncontactable
since flash floods and landslides struck Rasuwa District in Nepal on Aug 26. The floods also affected areas along the Nepal-Tibet border.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Grab's GX Bank calls for expansion of government-backed credit guarantees to digital lenders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: GXBank has called for the expansion of government-backed credit guarantees to digital lending platforms as part of efforts to improve financing access for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) under the 2027 Budget.
Its chief executive officer Kaushik Chowdhury said expanding guarantee schemes, including the proposed RM10 billion Bank Negara Malaysia-Credit Guarantee Corporation facility, to digital lenders would allow them to provide lower cost loans to MSMEs.
"By leveraging alternative underwriting data, such as real-time cash flows and e-commerce transactions, digital banks can safely deploy low-cost, collateral-free working capital to small businesses facing severe margin pressures," he said in a statement.
Kaushik said the 2027 Budget also presents an opportunity to reduce administrative and other frictions associated with micro-financing.
Building on the stamp duty relief for micro-financing introduced in the 2025 budget, he proposed extending targeted duty exemptions to small-ticket loans to reduce the disproportionate costs associated with lower-value borrowing.
"Digital banks can seamlessly pass these tax savings directly to hawkers, gig workers and MSMEs - lowering effective borrowing costs," he added.
Kaushik also called for greater integration between licensed digital banks and government digital infrastructure through direct, low-cost application programming interface connections.
Streamlining digital verification would reduce onboarding requirements and operational costs while expanding access to financial services among rural communities, gig workers and underserved groups, the digital bank said.
Separately, Kaushik proposed tax incentives and public matching grants for financial institutions investing in artificial intelligence-based fraud detection and scam prevention.
"Treating anti-scam protection as shared critical infrastructure ensures banks can maintain robust security without passing technology overhead costs down to lower-income consumers," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] 3,542 Myanmar detainees to be repatriated in second phase
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A total of 3,542 Myanmar detainees will be repatriated in the second phase, following the return of 1,476 people in the first phase.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the 1,476 detainees in the first group were identified by the
Myanmar authorities
.
He said their names were submitted to Malaysia through a diplomatic note dated Aug 13 via Wisma Putra.
"For the second phase, 3,542 Myanmar detainees have been agreed with Myanmar to be sent home at the next stage," he said at a post-cabinet meeting press conference here.
He said Wisma Putra would hold discussions with Myanmar soon so that more Myanmar detainees in Malaysia could be accepted back after the second batch was completed.
Fahmi added that Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing was set to make an official visit to Malaysia for talks next week.
Asked when the second batch would be repatriated, Fahmi said the government was waiting for Myanmar to give a date.
"At this point, we are waiting for Myanmar to give a date.
"This will be coordinated with the Home Ministry, which manages the depots where the Myanmar detainees are held, and Wisma Putra, which handles diplomatic notes from Myanmar," he said.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim defended Malaysia's engagement with Myanmar, saying calls to simply "not send them back" offered no solution for the hundreds of thousands of Myanmar people who fled the country to Malaysia.
He said Malaysia was seeking security guarantees for any returns, which was why Min Aung Hlaing had been invited for talks.
Thousands of people have fled Myanmar since a 2021 military coup that sparked a nationwide civil war.
The coup came after a widespread campaign of atrocity crimes by security forces in August 2017 against the Rohingya, who are not recognised as citizens despite their historical presence in Rakhine State.
The violence killed thousands and razed hundreds of villages across northern Rakhine.
As of February, Malaysia housed around 193,800 people who had fled Myanmar of various ethnicities, including Rohingya and Chin, according to UNHCR data. Activists, however, said many more remained unregistered.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US Senate blocks measure demanding report on rights violations in West Bank
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Senate Republicans on Tuesday blocked a bid to require President Donald Trump's administration to report to Congress on increasing violence in the occupied West Bank, including the deaths of American citizens.
The procedural vote was the latest sign of friction between US Democrats and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government over Israel's treatment of Palestinians and of Republicans' continuing strong support for his coalition.
The Senate voted 47 to 51 to block the resolution.
The vote was largely along party lines, with every Republican voting no except for Rand Paul of Kentucky and every Democrat except John Fetterman of Pennsylvania in favor.
The resolution would have required the State Department to report to Congress on the killing of US citizens by Israeli settlers or Israeli security forces in the West Bank and to assess the human rights situation.
Violence by Jewish settlers against Palestinians in the territory has risen sharply this year.
While the resolution would not have cut aid to Israel, the largest cumulative recipient of US foreign assistance since World War Two, a failure by the administration to deliver the report could have triggered restrictions on aid.
Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, the measure's lead sponsor, had argued that it was "long past time" to examine human rights in the West Bank, including the deaths of nine Americans since 2022.
"It is our responsibility to ensure recipients of US taxpayer dollars act in line with our laws and our values," he said in a statement, referring to Israel.
Republicans accused Democrats of seeking to score political points as Israel is under threat, seven months after US and Israeli forces launched airstrikes that began an ongoing conflict with Iran.
"I urge my colleagues to vote no on this resolution so we can stand with our ally Israel as they beat back the scourge of Iranian-backed terrorism," Montana Republican Senator Steve Daines said in a speech.
The vote took place weeks before US midterm elections on Nov 3, in which polls show Trump's Republicans could lose their congressional majorities, signaling a potential shift in Israel policy in the new Congress.
Polls show the war with Iran is not popular with Americans, who are frustrated with higher energy prices resulting from the conflict.
Netanyahu, who has long aligned himself with US Republicans, faces an election in Israel on Oct  27, which public opinion polls show his right-wing coalition could lose.
Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. The UN and most countries consider settlements there illegal under international law governing military occupation. Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.
Some Democrats — and a few ​Republicans — also have called for curbs on military aid to Israel over its conduct of the war in Gaza, with tens of thousands of Palestinians killed and much of the enclave in ruins.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 10 former Negri Sembilan excos vacate offices, return official vehicles
Article:
SEREMBAN: Ten former Negri Sembilan executive councillors whose appointments were revoked have stopped using their offices at Wisma Negeri and returned their official vehicles.
The move followed the gazetting of the revocation of their appointments on Sept 24, which took effect from Sept 20.
Former state Industry, Technology, Innovation and Digital Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, speaking on behalf of the former executive councillors, confirmed that they had received instructions from the State Secretary's Office to return their official vehicles.
"Since the gazette was issued, I have no longer used the official vehicle.
"We received a letter from the State Secretary instructing us to return the vehicles.
"We complied with the directive. Whatever the instruction is, we will follow it," said Asna, who is also Lenggeng assemblyman.
However, the former executive councillors' offices at Wisma Negeri continue to operate, with their officers and staff remaining at work.
"The former executive councillors no longer come to their offices at Wisma Negeri.
"All the assemblymen are operating from their respective state constituency service centres.
"Only we, the officers and staff, continue to carry out our duties here at Wisma Negeri," an officer attached to one of the former executive councillors said when contacted today.
The appointments of the 10 executive councillors were
officially revoked
with effect from Sept 20 with the consent of Negri Sembilan Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
The revocation was gazetted on Sept 24.
According to the gazette, the appointments were withdrawn after the 10 were found to have breached their pledges of allegiance following their actions in relation to a proclamation concerning Tuanku Muhriz's position as Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Police officers from Bukit Aman police
recorded statements
from the 10 former executive councillors as part of investigations into the matter.
Yesterday, Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap Seremban.
The meeting was understood to be related to the state administration and the ongoing situation.
Ismail has yet to issue any statement on the substance of the meeting or whether any decision was reached.
His press secretary, Mohd Fasha Musthafa, said there had so far been no instruction to issue a statement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johan Setia reports highest unhealthy API level at 166, twenty areas in total experiencing bad air
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Twenty areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4.30 pm today, with Johan Setia in Selangor registering the highest level at 166.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, four other areas in Selangor also recorded unhealthy air quality: Shah Alam (164), Klang (158), Petaling Jaya (155) and Banting (143).
Two monitoring stations in the capital recorded a similar trend, in Cheras (162) and Batu Muda (160), while Putrajaya registered 157.
In Johor, the affected areas were Pasir Gudang (164), Larkin (162), Kota Tinggi (155), Pengerang (152) and Kluang (110), while in Negeri Sembilan, they were Nilai (161) and Seremban (153).
Unhealthy readings were also recorded in Balok Baru and Indera Mahkota in Pahang, each at 156.
They were followed by Kuala Terengganu, Terengganu (154), Bandaraya Melaka, Melaka (125) and Kota Bharu, Kelantan (103).
Meanwhile, 45 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while only three were at a good level.
API readings of zero to 50 are categorised as good, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and above 300 (hazardous).  — Bernama

Title: Flying this weekend? Malaysia Airlines urges KLIA passengers to arrive early amid Sepang F1 traffic
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Malaysia Airlines advises passengers travelling from KL International Airport (KLIA) on Oct 2-4, 2026 to allow additional travel time to the airport, due to expected traffic congestion during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit.
The national airline said that while access to KLIA remains available, passengers are advised to monitor the latest traffic and road closure updates from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and plan alternative routes where necessary.
It also stated that passengers are encouraged to consider using the KLIA Ekspres service to reach the airport.
