Title: Sarawak hydrogen market viability still unproven, says analyst
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 30 — Putrajaya should think twice about extending incentives to Sarawak’s hydrogen sector when it has yet to prove that there are enough buyers willing to pay commercially viable prices, according to an analyst.
Samirul Ariff Othman from Global Asia Consulting said the concern was particularly relevant after Sarawak sought more Budget 2027 support for clean energy and other high-value industries, in a meeting this week between Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He said the basic problem with hydrogen was not Sarawak’s ability to produce it, but whether anyone wanted to buy enough of it at a price that made the business sustainable.
“You can build the plant and produce the hydrogen. But if you do not have customers willing to pay the price, you do not yet have a business. A production advantage matters only if enough of it survives delivery.”
The Energy Industries Council previously reported that Sarawak’s flagship export-oriented H2biscus and H2ornbill projects were scaled down following weak demand signals and uncertainty over securing buyers, while the state later acknowledged that the projects were also facing financial constraints.
The problem was particularly clear in the proposed Japanese market.
Sarawak Economic Development Corporation (SEDC) Energy chairman Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Husain said hydrogen could be produced in Sarawak for below RM20 per kg, but compression, cooling and transport pushed the delivered cost in Japan to around RM50 per kg. He said the original proposal to export all the hydrogen to Japan was therefore not viable unless support such as subsidies was provided in the buyer country.
Samirul said incentives made more sense where they helped an otherwise viable investment get across the line.
“If there is already a customer, an investor and a project that makes commercial sense, an incentive can help Malaysia win that investment. But if the market itself is not there yet, the government has to be much more careful because taxpayers are effectively taking the demand risk.”
As for domestic demand, Samirul noted that in August 2025, the Darul Hana hydrogen facility had a stated capacity of 150 kilogrammes a day and supplied ten fuel-cell vehicles. SEDC Energy’s chief executive acknowledged it was “uneconomical” to leave an operational plant underused.
According to Samirul, Sarawak is trying to boost domestic demand through publicly backed entities, specifically the Kuching Urban Transportation System. KUTS is expected to have around 38 hydrogen-powered ART vehicles and 55 hydrogen feeder buses.
“KUTS gives the hydrogen plant a buyer, but essentially the state is buying from itself,” he said.
“The state backs the producer, the state backs the transport operator and public money pays for the infrastructure. That may be useful to get the technology going, but it does not tell you whether other customers would choose hydrogen at that price.”
He added that this model also does not establish value for money.
“If a publicly backed producer sells hydrogen to a publicly backed transport operator, the financial assessment must cover both organisations. Revenue received by one may be expenditure supported by the state in another.”
Samirul said this did not mean Putrajaya should reject Sarawak’s request for clean-energy incentives altogether, such as in renewables.
“Some of these technologies and projects already have customers and proven economics. But for others, it would be better to see real buyers, binding offtake agreements and a clear idea of when the industry stops depending on the government to create demand before more support goes in.”
He added that even hydrogen, ammonia and methanol involve different processing requirements and markets. Each requires its own business case.
Returns on investment
Samirul said the wider question is how Sarawak converts resource wealth into lasting productive capacity. The 2026 state budget, for instance, allocated RM1 billion for ART infrastructure and systems.
“Sarawak receives substantial revenue from oil and gas, and that has given the state much more money to invest. So once you start putting that money into a new industry, the obvious question is: what are Sarawakians getting back?”
Samirul said emerging industries did not necessarily have to make an immediate profit, but governments should still be able to show why the investment was better than alternative uses of the same money.
“There has to be a credible path to a return. If the same ringgit could go into power, infrastructure or another industry where there are already customers waiting, then hydrogen has to show why it deserves that ringgit instead,” he added.
“Capital has alternative uses. So does electricity. Hydropower allocated to hydrogen could potentially serve other industries, households or electricity sales.”
He added that the evidence available supports disciplined experimentation and fuller disclosure.
“It does not establish that Sarawak’s hydrogen strategy has failed. Equally, strategic promise cannot substitute indefinitely for demonstrable results.”

Title: Immigration Dept denies social media claim that Myanmar teen was repatriated, says she remains in detention
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The Immigration Department today denied claims that a Myanmar teenage girl was among those repatriated to Myanmar yesterday, saying she remains in custody at an immigration detention depot.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said checks by the department found that the teenager was not involved in the September 29 repatriation programme, which saw Myanmar nationals transported home aboard Myanmar naval vessels.
“Checks by the department confirmed that the individual remains detained at an Immigration depot and was not involved in the repatriation programme for Myanmar nationals via Myanmar military vessels yesterday,” he said in a statement.
The department said the clarification followed a viral social-media post alleging that the Myanmar teenager had been sent back under the programme, although it did not identify the account behind the post or provide further details about the girl.
The claim emerged as Malaysia yesterday began repatriating 1,476 Myanmar detainees from 14 immigration depots, comprising 1,370 men, 79 women, 20 boys and seven girls.
Zakaria said the department was aware of concerns over the safety and welfare of detainees, adding that humanitarian considerations were taken into account in enforcing immigration laws and procedures.
The department also said immigration depots were managed in accordance with the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners, or Nelson Mandela Rules, as well as domestic regulations governing immigration depots.
It urged the public not to circulate unverified information that could cause confusion over the department’s actions and procedures.

Title: Myanmar man gets 16 years’ prison for killing 80-year-old fruit seller in Taman OUG
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — A Myanmar man was sentenced to 16 years’ imprisonment by the High Court today after pleading guilty to causing the death of an elderly fruit seller at a house in Taman OUG, three years ago.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin handed down the sentence on Shofi Husson Fozo Rahman, 29, and ordered the accused to serve the prison term from the date of his arrest on Sept 26, 2023.
He was charged with causing the death of Ah Kau @ Yow Chow Chong, 80, at 6.30 pm on Sept 26, 2023, under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 30 years and a fine.
Based on the facts of the case, the victim had gone to the house to collect fruit for sale before an argument broke out between the two men. The accused then took a knife and stabbed the victim in the neck and body.
CCTV footage showed the victim at the scene before the accused approached him and threw an object believed to be a knife as he left the scene.
A post-mortem found that the victim had sustained six stab wounds, including two to the neck that penetrated muscle and major blood vessels, causing serious bleeding, as well as a wound to the left forearm.
Earlier, deputy public prosecutor Faridah Nurdinie Bahrum sought a deterrent sentence that would serve as a lesson to the accused and society at large.
“Although the victim was 80 years old, he was still working, and the scene was where he kept his fruit. He was a father, and his death had a profound impact on his family. As a foreign national, the accused should have complied with the laws of this country,” she said.
Meanwhile, the accused’s lawyer Datuk C. Vignesh Kumar sought a prison sentence of between 12 and 15 years, taking into account his client’s guilty plea, which spared the court’s time and costs
He added that his client has no prior criminal record and supports a wife and a child.
“The accused behaved well while in prison. His experience in prison has had a profound effect on him. He also apologises and is remorseful for his actions,” said the lawyer. — Bernama

Title: Primary Six pupil suffers burns after setting off firecrackers, Muar cops probe social media influence
Article:
MUAR, Sept 30 — A Primary Six pupil, believed to have been influenced by action and high-intensity content on social media, suffered burns after setting off firecrackers at a school here yesterday.
The incident also triggered panic among parents and the school community.
Muar police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said the 12-year-old boy was injured in the incident, which occurred at about 11am.
“The pupil involved was then taken to Sultanah Fatimah Specialist Hospital (HPSF) here for treatment.
“A preliminary psychiatric assessment was also conducted on the pupil before he was allowed to continue treatment as an outpatient.
“Examinations revealed that the victim suffered burns on several parts of his body and is currently receiving treatment,” he said in a statement today.
Raiz Mukhliz said initial investigations later led police to detain the pupil to assist in the probe.
He said investigations suggested the pupil was likely influenced by action and high-intensity content on social media and the internet.
“However, further investigations are being conducted to identify all the factors that led to the incident.
“A search was also conducted at the scene and the pupil’s residence where several items believed to be linked to the incident were seized for further investigation and analysis,” he said.
Raiz Mukhliz said six witnesses had come forward to assist investigators, while efforts to locate other witnesses were ongoing.
He said the school acted proactively immediately after the incident by directing pupils to a safe area before seeking police assistance.
A safety inspection was also carried out at the scene by the Muar district police bomb disposal unit, while the Johor police contingent’s forensic unit conducted a forensic examination.
“Checks and inspections found no other explosive threats in the vicinity of the incident,” he said.
Earlier, the pupil was brought before the Magistrate's Court, where police obtained a four-day remand order until Saturday to facilitate investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 436 of the Penal Code for mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to damage, as well as Sections 6 and 8 of the Explosives Act 1957.

Title: Selangor mulls appeal after High Court finds authorities liable for 2021 Taman Sri Muda floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The Selangor government is considering whether to appeal a High Court ruling that found the federal government and two state authorities liable for negligence over the devastating 2021 Taman Sri Muda floods.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the state would first seek advice from the State Legal Adviser before deciding its next step,
Berita Harian
reported today.
“(We will examine) whether an appeal should be filed or otherwise, because this is only a High Court decision and there is still room for an appeal to provide justification,” he was quoted as saying.
He was speaking after the launch of the Selangor Roads and Highways Strategic Plan 2026-2035 (JALUR Selangor) here.
The High Court yesterday ruled in favour of 50 Taman Sri Muda residents who sued the government and several public authorities over losses they suffered during the catastrophic floods in December 2021.
Judicial Commissioner Shoba Rajah Dorai Rajah found the federal government, the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) and Shah Alam City Council (MBSA), among the defendants, liable for negligence and related failures that contributed to the residents’ losses.
The residents alleged failures in flood management, drainage systems, weather warnings and disaster response.
The court held the liable defendants jointly and severally responsible for the losses suffered by the residents.
The residents are seeking RM3,767,148.51 in special damages, as well as general and aggravated damages.
The High Court has fixed October 6 for case management to determine a date for the assessment of damages.
Taman Sri Muda in Shah Alam was among the areas worst affected by the widespread floods of December 2021, which left residents stranded as floodwaters rose rapidly.

Title: DOE: Over 500 hotspots in Kalimantan and Sumatra behind haze in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The haze currently affecting the country is caused by moderate to thick smoke from clusters of hotspots detected across much of Kalimantan as well as central and southern Sumatra.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) reported 327 hotspots in Kalimantan and another 191 in Sumatra yesterday, while one hotspot was detected in Sarawak.
“ASMC also reported moderate transboundary haze affecting several areas in Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore and northwestern Borneo,” she said in a statement today.
She said the DOE had stepped up inspections, patrols and monitoring in fire-prone areas, particularly peatlands and landfill sites, amid continued hot and dry weather.
“Where offences are identified, follow-up action will be taken based on the findings of inspections and investigations, as well as evidence obtained on the ground,” she said.
Azuri Azizah said the DOE would continue monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, hotspots and transboundary haze developments, taking meteorological information into account when assessing the situation and coordinating haze management measures at district, state and national levels.
As of 2 pm today, 23 areas in Peninsular Malaysia recorded unhealthy API readings, with the highest readings reported in several states, including Selangor, Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
She said DOE measures were being carried out in an integrated manner under the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK), which sets out the roles of various agencies according to the severity and development of the haze situation.
The department would also regularly provide updates on the situation, monitoring and patrol findings, Open Burning Prevention Operations (OMPT) and enforcement actions in accordance with the established reporting mechanism.
She said this was to ensure the situation could be assessed continuously and appropriate measures coordinated at all levels.
The DOE also stressed the need for cooperation from the industrial sector to reduce air emissions from major sources, particularly in areas where API readings exceed 300. — Bernama

Title: ‘Dinner, but no deal yet’: Fahmi says nothing formal between Pakatan and Bersatu for now
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — Pakatan Harapan has yet to begin formal discussions with Bersatu over possible cooperation for the Melaka state election, despite a closed-door meeting between representatives of both sides earlier this week.
PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said any decision on political cooperation would have to be made by the coalition's presidential council, adding that he had not received any information on formal negotiations with Bersatu.
“So far, there have been no developments (on the cooperation). I have yet to receive any information on the matter,” he told reporters yesterday.
His comments came after PH and Bersatu leaders attended a closed-door dinner in Melaka on Monday night, fuelling speculation that the two sides could be exploring an electoral arrangement ahead of the state election.
However, acting Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim described the gathering as an opportunity to maintain cordial ties, while Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said it was an informal session to get to know one another and exchange views.
PH has also indicated that it is open to discussions with other parties, with Adam saying the coalition was still waiting for PAS to extend an invitation for talks.
“PAS is the only one that has not invited us yet and I am waiting too,” he was reported as saying.
The developments come as political parties consider their respective electoral arrangements before the Election Commission meets on October 7 to determine key dates for the 16th Melaka state election.
The EC said the special meeting will decide, among other matters, the writ of election, nomination day, polling day and the electoral roll to be used.
The Melaka state assembly was dissolved on September 23.

Title: Fahmi: Govt expects F1, KL Marathon and Le Tour de Langkawi to go ahead despite haze
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — The government expects the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Le Tour de Langkawi and Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon to proceed this weekend despite haze affecting several parts of the country, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the haze situation was being monitored on a day-to-day basis, with the Youth and Sports Ministry (KBS) expected to make decisions on the events based on prevailing conditions.
“For now, the government expects the three major events — LTdL, F1 and the Standard Chartered Marathon — to continue,” he said during a press conference here.
Fahmi said the Cabinet had also discussed the haze situation ahead of the three major sporting events, while Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had raised the issue during his recent meeting with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.
He said Malaysia had also offered assets to Indonesia to help the country tackle fires contributing to the regional haze.
“We hope the haze can be controlled. From day to day there has been some rain, but at the same time KBS (Ministry of Youth and Sports) will make the decision,” he said.
Fahmi said Malaysia would continue to follow official channels in dealing with Indonesia on the haze issue, including through the Foreign Ministry.
He said Malaysia was still awaiting a response to a note sent through Wisma Putra concerning the issue.
The three major sporting events are scheduled to take place this weekend, with the Formula One race at the Sepang International Circuit, LTdL stages taking place in several states and the Standard Chartered Marathon in Kuala Lumpur.
The haze has pushed air quality into the unhealthy range in several parts of the country, raising concerns over athletes, spectators and event personnel taking part in prolonged outdoor activities.

Title: Touch ‘n Go to add 10 Enhanced RFID lanes for Malaysia’s MLFF transition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Touch ‘n Go Sdn Bhd (Touch ‘n Go) is expanding its Enhanced Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) network with 10 additional lanes by the end of the year to support the country’s transition towards a Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) tolling ecosystem.
Its Chief Operations Officer Liza Woon Yin Yin said the expansion, announced in conjunction with Touch ‘n Go’s 30th anniversary, aligns with the company’s broader vision to support the government’s barrier-free tolling initiative by providing robust and proven technology.
“We are ready to support with the technology, and we’ll continuously improve. We have a total of 10 more new lanes by the end of the year to support and prove the technology that we have to ease up the whole toll mobility,” she told Bernama when met at the MyASEAN Roads & Traffic Tech Expo (MyARTTE) at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) here today.
The new lanes will be deployed across five highways, comprising two lanes each at the Putrajaya Toll Plaza on the Maju Expressway (MEX), Sungai Ramal Toll Plaza on the Kajang Dispersal Link Expressway (SILK), Bukit Raja Toll Plaza on the Grand Sepadu Highway, and Bukit Jelutong Toll Plaza on the Guthrie Corridor Expressway (GCE).
Another two lanes, one each, will be installed at the Sungai Long and Ampang Toll Plazas on the East Klang Valley Expressway (EKVE).
Currently, two Enhanced RFID lanes are already operational, located at the Ampang-bound Dato Keramat toll plaza on AKLEH, and the Putrajaya-bound Putrajaya toll plaza on the MEX Highway.
Woon said the RFID lanes feature an enhanced technology that utilises two RFID antennas paired with an Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) camera.
“It’s an enhanced technology with two RFID antennas, and together with the ANPR camera in the middle to support the front and also the back as a secondary RFID to strengthen the security and also the accuracy,” she said.
Woon also assured motorists of a much smoother drive-through experience, noting that the upgraded lanes will offer an experience similar to the targeted MLFF system.
Earlier, she took the media on a guided tour of Touch ‘n Go’s Connected Mobility pavilion, themed “Future of Malaysia’s Mobility, Built on 30 Years of Trust”.
Woon shared insights into the company’s 30-year milestone and technological advancements, while briefing the media on the Single Lane Fast Flow (SLFF) e-RFID, MLFF Titan Flow technology and Gold Star virtual reality (VR) experience.
Meanwhile, Touch ‘n Go, in a statement, said the 10 new Enhanced RFID lanes will be clearly indicated by a gold star symbol on the lane signage to help motorists identify them easily.
Unlike conventional lanes, the Enhanced RFID lanes incorporate components of Touch ‘n Go’s homegrown Titan Flow technology stack, combining enhanced RFID capabilities with artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning technologies.
This multi-technology approach significantly improves vehicle detection and lane throughput, enabling highly reliable toll transactions even at higher vehicle speeds. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Malaysia needs young talent to navigate diverse challenges
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — The country needs a younger generation with determination, understanding and knowledge to take on the important responsibilities of driving national development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said young people with such talent and leadership qualities were essential in navigating the various challenges and complexities of the country’s governance.
"When you are in the public service, you will see how diverse and complex the issues we face are.
"We have people of different races, religions, regions and backgrounds, all expecting the very best from us. But, God willing, we can do our best,” he said in his speech at the 2026 MADANI Fellowship Programme here today.
Also present were Deputy Prime Ministers Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, and Cabinet ministers. — Bernama

Title: KTM Komuter, ETS services resume after Batang Benar-Labu power line repairs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — KTM Komuter Klang Valley and ETS services have resumed normal operations after repair works on the overhead power line between Batang Benar and Labu were completed at 1.41pm today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) said.
In a statement, KTMB said KTM Komuter and ETS services on the Pulau Sebang-Batu Caves-Pulau Sebang route were operating as usual, although some ETS journeys could still face temporary delays as train movements and schedules are readjusted.
KTMB thanked passengers for their patience and apologised for the inconvenience caused by the disruption.
Earlier today,
Malay Mail
reported that services were disrupted from 6.24am after a 25kV overhead power line between Batang Benar and Labu was severed.
Preliminary checks indicated that an animal was suspected of coming into contact with both a live wire and an earth wire, triggering the electrical fault.

Title: Free Rapid KL shuttle buses to Sepang circuit to run every 10–15 minutes from Oct 2–4
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Rapid KL will operate free shuttle bus services to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from October 2 to 4, with buses running every 10 to 15 minutes from three pick-up points.
According to travel information released by Rapid KL, passengers can board the direct service at KLIA 2, Bandar Baru Enstek and Mitsui Outlet Park.
The shuttle will operate from 7am until midnight on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, with frequencies subject to traffic conditions.
At KLIA 2, passengers can board at the Level 1 bus hub at Bays B1, B2 and B3.
The Bandar Baru Enstek pick-up and drop-off point is at De-Village, Persiaran Millenia 2, while passengers using Mitsui Outlet Park can board at its bus hub.
Rapid KL also provided travel guidance for passengers connecting from its rail network.
Those travelling on the Kelana Jaya Line or KL Monorail can head to KL Sentral before taking either the KLIA Ekspres or KLIA Transit to KLIA 2.
Passengers on the Kajang Line can similarly travel via KL Sentral or Muzium Negara before connecting to the airport rail service.
Those using the Ampang/Sri Petaling Line can change at Bandar Tasik Selatan and take KLIA Transit to KLIA 2, while Putrajaya Line passengers can connect to KLIA Transit at Putrajaya Sentral.
From KLIA 2, passengers can board the free Rapid KL shuttle to the Sepang International Circuit.

Title: Kuala Pilah school death: Five students allege bullying by 16-year-old suspect
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 30 — Five students have come forward to police claiming they had been bullied by the first suspect detained over the death of a Form Two male student in Kuala Pilah last Friday.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the matter came to light as a result of further investigations into the 69 witness statements recorded so far.
“From the interrogations and during the recording of statements, five students claimed they had been bullied by the first suspect detained to assist in the case.
“So far, no new arrests have been made apart from the two male suspects, both aged 16, who are currently remanded until Oct 1 and 3, respectively, to assist in the investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code,” he told reporters via WhatsApp today.
He also disclosed that investigations had found that the victim had never informed his family that he had been bullied at school.
The media reported that police had detained another 16-year-old male student yesterday in the investigation into the death of a Form Two student in Kuala Pilah last Friday.
The first suspect, a Form Four student, had earlier been remanded for six days to assist in the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
On Sept 25, a Form Two student was injured in an incident at a school in Kuala Pilah. He later died at Hospital Tuanku Ampuan Najihah. — Bernama

Title: Lim Guan Eng calls for MACC action on Zahid over RM2.1b ministry overspending, cites UiTM precedent
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to initiate an investigation into Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi over an alleged RM2.1 billion budget overrun at the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW).
In a statement today, Lim said the anti-graft agency should apply the same rigorous enforcement standards to KKDW as it did in its recent probe into Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), where management was found to have channelled nearly RM260 million into its investment arm, UiTM Holdings, without the required approval from the Ministry of Finance.
Citing official Finance Ministry figures, Lim noted that KKDW spent RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an approved budget of RM1.1 billion. In 2024, the ministry expended RM2 billion against a RM1.3 billion allocation, followed by RM2.3 billion spent against an approved RM1.6 billion in 2025.
Lim said that the cumulative overspending totalled RM2.1 billion across the three-year period, all during Ahmad Zahid’s tenure as rural and regional development minister, stressing that unapproved overspending had not occurred prior to 2023.
“Such conduct by Ahmad Zahid Hamidi is irresponsible as it violates existing financial procedures and regulations, which could warrant enforcement under the relevant laws,” he said, adding that decisive action is essential to deter other federal ministries from committing similar fiscal breaches.
Lim warned that the MACC risks facing public accusations of selective prosecution and double standards if it hesitates to act against Ahmad Zahid and KKDW “because of his high position”, calling such inaction fundamentally unfair to the management of UiTM.
Lim pointed to findings by Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC), which discovered that UiTM management injected approximately RM260 million into UiTM Holdings in stages between 2007 and 2018 without Treasury clearance, resulting in accumulated losses of RM157.04 million across financial years 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2021.
According to the PAC, RM42 million designated for a 50-megawatt solar development in Gambang, Pahang, was diverted for unrelated operational expenses without the authorisation of the company’s board of directors.
Lim added that strict governance is needed to safeguard UiTM’s increased RM3.08 billion budget allocation for 2026.
The DAP advisor’s statement comes on the heels of enforcement action by the MACC over the financial losses at UiTM Holdings.
The commission confirmed that a former senior corporate executive in his 50s was arrested at his residence in the Klang Valley on Sept 28 and is expected to be charged in court this Thursday.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect allegedly authorised operational expense payments in 2017 amounting to approximately RM42 million to several companies in which he held a beneficial interest.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest, stating that the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009 for abuse of power to obtain gratification.

Title: No deal with Pakatan: Azmin says Bersatu preparing to contest Melaka polls alone
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia has ruled out working with Pakatan Harapan (PH) or any other political party in the Melaka state election, with secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali saying the party is preparing to contest on its own.
Azmin also said Bersatu intended to contest under its own logo, as it did in the Negeri Sembilan state election,
Berita Harian
reported today.
He said the party was now drawing up its election strategy and preparing its machinery for a solo campaign.
“Bersatu has not made any decision to cooperate with any party.
“The focus now is on reviewing preparations for election operations in several key areas,” he was quoted as saying.
Azmin’s remarks came amid speculation over a possible electoral arrangement with PH after senior figures from the two sides attended a private dinner in Melaka on Monday.
He said the meeting had no connection to Bersatu’s official position and was instead attended by those involved in their personal capacities.
“The meeting has nothing to do with the position of the Bersatu Political Bureau. It was a meeting held in a personal capacity,” he said.
Berita Harian
reported yesterday that several Bersatu leaders had met senior Melaka PH figures at a closed-door dinner held in conjunction with a pre-election programme at a hotel in Melaka.
Among those present were Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz, Melaka Bersatu election director Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamad, Bersatu associate wing chief Datuk Seri R Sanjeevan and Melaka Bersatu information chief Datuk Seri Hishamiddin Abdul Karim.
The meeting fuelled speculation about possible cooperation between the two blocs as parties negotiate their arrangements ahead of the state election.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari had said earlier this month that the coalition was holding talks with parties sharing similar aspirations, including Bersatu, over a possible “PH Plus” arrangement.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari subsequently described such an arrangement as more likely to take the form of an electoral understanding than a formal coalition.
The Melaka state assembly was dissolved on September 23. The Election Commission is due to meet on October 7 to determine the key dates for the election.

Title: Honda Civic driver gets attempted murder charge for ramming policeman at Ipoh roadblock
Article:
IPOH, Sept 30 — A car wash worker pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of attempting to murder a traffic policeman on Sept 24.
K. Viknes, 29, entered the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Norhayati Mohamad Yunus.
According to the charge sheet, Viknes, who was driving a Honda Civic, attempted to murder Lance Corporal Badrul Izwany Pauzi, 29, by ramming the vehicle into the victim, knowing that the act could result in death.
The charge was framed under Section 307 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of up to 20 years and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor M. Raveena proposed bail of RM100,000, taking into account that the victim was a public servant performing his duties at the time of the incident, and requested that the accused surrender his passport pending disposal of the case.
However, lawyer Jagdave Singh, representing the accused, requested lower bail of RM10,000, saying his client earns only RM50 a day and is the sole breadwinner supporting his mother and two school-going siblings.
Judge Norhayati set bail at RM20,000 with one surety, subject to additional conditions, including that the accused report to the nearest police station once a month, not interfere with witnesses and surrender his passport to the court.
The court fixed Oct 26 for mention.
Badrul Izwany reportedly suffered a broken left arm and right leg on Sept 24 after being struck by a car driven by a man allegedly attempting to evade a police roadblock. The incident later went viral on social media. — Bernama

Title: Tanjung Rambutan care centre resident charged with murdering fellow patient
Article:
IPOH, Sept 30 — A man was charged in the Magistrates’ Court here today with murdering a resident of a care centre in Tanjung Rambutan, near here, on Sept 3.
The court, however, recorded no plea from Soo Kim Keong, 51, who is also a resident of the care centre, after the charge was read out before Magistrate Norizan Riduan, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
Kim Keong is accused of murdering Chong Mun Long, 28, at the Grace Home Care Centre, Jalan Chemor, Tanjung Rambutan, between 3 am and 4 am on the said day.
He is charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and, if the death penalty is not imposed, shall also be punished with not less than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
The magistrate ordered him to be referred to Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, Tanjung Rambutan, for psychiatric examination and fixed Oct 30 for the next case mention and submission of the psychiatric report.
Deputy public prosecutor Kirthana Subramanian appeared for the prosecution, while the accused is unrepresented.
On Sept 3, the victim was reported to have been found unconscious at the care centre, allegedly due to a misunderstanding with another resident.
He later died on Sept 17 at Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun due to a lung infection and blunt-force trauma to the head. — Bernama

Title: In Johor Bahru, man’s reversing mishap sends car into two vehicles and an eatery
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 — A 69-year-old man accidentally crashed his Toyota Camry into two vehicles and an eatery after apparently pressing the accelerator by mistake while reversing in Taman Daya here yesterday.
Johor Bahru South police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffie said police were alerted to the incident after videos of it went viral on social media at about 2.20pm.
He said preliminary investigations found that the local man was about to drive home after having breakfast at an eatery in Jalan Daya when the incident occurred.
“While attempting to reverse his Toyota Camry car, the man is believed to have mistakenly accelerated the car’s pedal, causing the vehicle to jolt backward and crashed into a Proton Saga parked behind him.
“Following the initial collision, the man panicked and floored the accelerator again, causing the vehicle to reverse further and crashed into another white Toyota Camry located in front of the eatery.
The aftermath of an accident at an eatery in Taman Daya, Johor Bahru, after a Toyota Camry crashed into two vehicles before ploughing into the premises on September 29, 2026. — Screengrab via Facebook/Bikram Nisturi
“The affected vehicles continued moving before crashing and coming to a stop inside of the eatery’s premises,” he said in a statement late last night.
The two other cars and the eatery were damaged in the incident, but no injuries were reported.
Azrul Hisham said the incident was believed to have been caused by the driver’s negligence while operating the accelerator, resulting in him losing control of the vehicle.
The case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Videos and images showing the aftermath of the accident were circulated on social media yesterday.
A similar accident occurred about two weeks ago in Pandan Perdana, Ampang Jaya, where an 89-year-old driver allegedly pressed the accelerator while attempting to park, causing his vehicle to hit a motorcyclist, a flower seller and a pedestrian.
In the September 12 incident, all three victims reportedly sustained injuries and received treatment at a nearby hospital.

Title: ‘We are always open’: BN still negotiating political cooperation, says Asyraf Wajdi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said talks over Barisan Nasional’s (BN) approach to the Melaka state election are still ongoing, with its political cooperation arrangements yet to be finalised.
According to
Utusan Malaysia
, Asyraf said discussions remained at the leadership level and noted that the Election Commission had yet to announce the election date.
“We are still negotiating. Let’s wait. The Election Commission has not even announced the date yet,” he was quoted as saying after officiating the Mara Automotive Ecosystem (MATEC) 2026 here today.
Asked whether BN was considering a new political alignment, he said the coalition remained on the same course.
“If they (Pakatan Harapan) do not want to cooperate, that is their right. We cannot force them because it is their party, not ours. We are always open,” he said.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh had said on Sunday that BN would begin talks with other political groupings ahead of the 16th Melaka state election.
He said the discussions would include BN’s position that it should defend the 21 state seats it won in the 2021 election.
However,
Utusan Malaysia
subsequently reported that no meeting between BN and other political groupings took place at Menara Dato’ Onn on Monday as initially expected.

Title: College student fails to strike out murder charge over Jalan Ampang collision that killed couple
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — A college student today failed in his bid to have a murder charge against him struck out in connection with the deaths of a married couple in a collision on Jalan Ampang, near Great Eastern Mall here, four months ago.
High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the ruling after allowing the prosecution’s preliminary objection to the application filed by Danish Raman Kamar Kumaresan on August 5.
“After examining the submissions of both parties, the court allows the prosecution’s preliminary objection. Accordingly, the accused’s application to strike out the murder charge is dismissed,” said the judge.
Today’s proceedings were attended by deputy public prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry and lawyer Donald Selvam, who represented Danish Raman.
The prosecution raised the preliminary objection on the grounds that the applicant’s bid to strike out the charge was irregular and did not comply with the provisions under the Courts of Judicature Act 1964.
Danish Raman, 24, sought to have the charge struck out, arguing that the prosecution’s decision to charge him under Section 302 of the Penal Code for a road accident case was mala fide, that is, in bad faith.
He further contended that the decision was unreasonable and in breach of Articles 5 and 8 of the Federal Constitution.
On May 15, Danish Raman was charged at the Magistrates’ Court here with the murder of senior citizen A. Doraisingam, 61, and his wife A. Menagah, 56, on Jalan Ampang, travelling from the direction of KLCC towards Ampang Point, at 5.30am on May 2.
The couple died from severe head injuries after the Honda Wave Alpha motorcycle they were riding was struck from behind by a Toyota Vios driven by the man.
He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, and a minimum of 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash: Police find no indication of foul play
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 30 — Police have found no indication of foul play in their investigation into the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash at Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, which claimed five lives, with the probe now nearing completion.
Bukit Aman Management director and Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said police had taken statements from several witnesses, including those connected to locations visited by the crew members and the helicopter before the incident.
“So far, we have not found anything that indicates what actually caused the incident.
“As for other elements, including foul play and so on, we have not seen any indication of that,” he told reporters after officiating at the Sarawak Police Commissioner’s Monthly Assembly at the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters here on Wednesday.
Mohamad Zainal said a technical problem was among the possible causes being considered, but the actual cause would be determined by the Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB).
He added that the bureau had the expertise to determine the actual cause of the crash and was expected to announce its findings within 30 days at the earliest.
“So I cannot comment on the other matters. As far as the police investigation is concerned, we have nearly completed our investigation,” he said.
The FDS helicopter crashed at the Long Lellang STOLport at around 3.40pm on September 8 with five crew members, including the pilot, on board.
The victims were identified as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; as well as staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — The Borneo Post

Title: Bidor petrol station shooting: Man hospitalised with bullet wound to shoulder
Article:
TAPAH, Sept 30 — A 41-year-old man was reportedly shot in the left shoulder after two gunmen opened fire on his four-wheel-drive vehicle at a petrol station in Bidor Sentral yesterday.
According to
Berita Harian
, Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the incident occurred at about 6.08pm after the victim drove his white Toyota Land Cruiser into the station to refuel.
“Two men believed to be armed with firearms got out of the car and fired several shots at the victim’s vehicle before fleeing,” Mohd Alwi was quoted as saying, adding that a black Honda City had stopped in front of the Land Cruiser shortly beforehand.
The victim, who was struck by one bullet, was initially taken to Tapah Hospital before being transferred to hospitals in Ipoh, including Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital, and is reported to be in stable condition.
Police forensic investigators reportedly recovered one 9mm Luger bullet, four spent cartridge cases of the same calibre and bullet fragments at the scene, while further fragments and bullet marks were found on the victim’s vehicle.
Mohd Alwi said investigators were reviewing CCTV footage from locations around Bidor and identified toll plazas as they work to establish the identities of the suspects and the motive for the shooting.
The case is being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code and Section 3(1) of the Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971.

Title: Man jailed two weeks for trespassing at house linked to Sarawak deputy premier’s wife
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 30 — A 21-year-old man was sentenced to two weeks’ jail and fined RM1,500 in default one month’s imprisonment by the Magistrates’ Court here today for trespassing at a house under the control of Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan’s wife.
Magistrate Nureina Syafika Mohd Najib meted out the sentence on Haiqal Haqimi Sumardi after he pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 447 of the Penal Code.
The section provides for imprisonment of up to six months, a fine of up to RM3,000, or both.
The offence was committed at 9.50am on September 24 at a single-storey house in Taman Sri Sena under the control of Datuk Dayang Morliah Datuk Awang Daud.
According to the facts of the case, a complainant, who is Dayang Morliah’s brother, noticed the accused entering the house without any permission.
A police report was lodged, and investigations led to the accused’s arrest the following day, September 25.
It is learnt that the incident had gone viral on social media, with the accused believed to have intended to steal items from the house to sell in order to buy drugs.
It is also understood that the accused tested positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Muhammad Aidil Akmal Sharidan appeared for the prosecution while the accused was unrepresented. The case was investigated by Sgt Daniel Bong. The accused (front row, second right) is seen at Kuching Court Complex today. — The Borneo Post

Title: Negeri Sembilan PKR urges swift end to state administrative impasse
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 30 — The Negeri Sembilan Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Leadership Council has called for the state’s institutional and administrative impasse to be resolved swiftly to ensure government affairs and the people’s interests are not further affected.
Its chairman, Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun, said the developments involved not only constitutional and royal institutional issues but also raised concerns over the continuity of the state administration, economic stability and public welfare.
The former menteri besar said uncertainty over the status of members of the State Executive Council (Exco) could delay important matters requiring consideration and approval by the state authorities.
“Investment and development matters, as well as land approvals and transfers and project implementation, could be affected. This could undermine investor confidence, complicate matters for landowners and businesses, and affect employment and household incomes.
“The appointment and functions of Village Development and Security Committees (JPKK) and councillors also cannot remain in limbo, as both serve as links between the government and the people at grassroots level. Their absence risks weakening representation and effective coordination,” he said in a Facebook post today.
The Port Dickson Member of Parliament said the situation had also created a perception that the state government was not functioning effectively due to the prolonged dispute.
Aminuddin said all political leaders should exercise restraint, avoid statements that could heighten tensions and allow constitutional and legal processes to resolve the crisis.
Yesterday, Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had an audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawi,r for nearly three hours at Istana Hinggap here.
The meeting was understood to have followed issues related to the state’s administration and the ongoing situation.
Tuanku Muhriz had previously revoked the appointments of 10 members of the state’s Exco, effective September 20. The revocation was gazetted on September 24.
The affected exco members are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah. — Bernama

Title: Babies born in Malaysia in 2026 expected to live 75.5 years, DOSM says
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — A baby born in 2026 is expected to live until the age of 75.5, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).
Citing its Abridged Life Tables, Malaysia 2024-2026, released today, DOSM said a baby girl is on average expected to live up to 78.1 years, 4.9 years longer than a baby boy, at 73.2 years.
“The highest life expectancy at birth for males and females by state for the period of 2024 to 2026 was recorded in Selangor, while Terengganu recorded the lowest.
“Three states exceeded the national level life expectancy (75.5 years) for 2026, namely Selangor (78.2 years), W.P. Kuala Lumpur (77.3 years) and W.P. Labuan (77.0 years),” the statement read.
DOSM said life expectancy at birth in 2019 rose 0.4 years compared with 2016, with male life expectancy increasing from 72.1 to 72.5 years and female life expectancy also up by 0.4 years.
Meanwhile, DOSM said life expectancy at birth in 2019 rose 0.4 years compared with 2016, with male life expectancy up from 72.1 to 72.5 years and female life expectancy also rising 0.4 years.
“However, in 2022, life expectancy at birth decreased by 0.9 years, with male life expectancy falling by 1.0 year and female life expectancy down by 0.8 years compared with 2020. In 2026, life expectancy at birth increased by 1.5 years compared with 2023.”
“The increase in life expectancy is due to the lower number of deaths from 2023 to 2026 as compared to the 2020 to 2022 period, which was attributed to excess deaths during the Covid-19 pandemic,” the statement read.
DOSM said males aged 15 and 60 years in 2026 are expected to live another 59.0 years and 18.9 years, respectively.
“This indicates that males aged 15 and 60 years in 2026 are expected to live until the age of 74.0 years and 78.9 years, respectively.
“On the other hand, females in the same age groups are expected to live for another 63.7 years and 21.7 years, with life expectancy of 78.7 years and 81.7 years, respectively,” the statement added. — Bernama

Title: MMEA ends One Fathom Bank search after recovering last body in Perak
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 30 — The body of the remaining angler reported missing at One Fathom Bank near Pulau Ketam on Sept 14 was found in waters off Kuala Kurau, Perak, yesterday.
Selangor MMEA director Maritime Captain Abdul Muhaimin Muhammad Salleh said the body of Raja Mohd Rozi Raja Mohamud, 49, was found floating by local fishermen about 4.5 nautical miles southwest of the Kuala Kurau estuary at 5.25 pm.
He said the fishermen alerted the Kuala Kurau Maritime Zone after spotting the body, which was wearing a blue shirt and camouflage trousers.
“The MMEA vessel Benteng 03 was then dispatched to the location and the body was taken to the Kuala Kurau Marine Police Jetty at 7.30 pm.
“The victim’s body was handed over to the police before being taken to the Taiping Hospital Forensic Medicine Department for formal identification,” he said in a statement today.
Abdul Muhaimin said Raja Mohd Rozi was identified by his wife based on the clothes he was wearing.
“The discovery of the final victim means the search for all seven victims involved in the incident is now over,” he said, while thanking rescue teams from various agencies and the local fishing community for their assistance and information throughout the search and rescue (SAR) operation.
Selangor MMEA launched the operation on Sept 14 after receiving a report at 3.35 am on the disappearance of seven anglers at One Fathom Bank.
The six-day operation covered an area of 3,887 square nautical miles in the waters of Selangor and Perak, including Hutan Melintang and Bagan Datuk.
On Sept 19, the operation was called off after no new leads were found.
Four victims survived the incident, while two others, identified as Muhammad Ridzuan Ruhaizat, 37, and Mohamad Shahril Abd Rahman, 43, were found dead in waters off Hutan Melintang. — Bernama

Title: Johor court fines 15 men, including Chinese nationals, over fake job scam aimed at US citizens
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 — Fifteen members of a job scam syndicate targeting US citizens were fined between RM3,500 and RM4,200 each by the Magistrate’s Court here today after pleading guilty to conspiring to commit fraud through non-existent job offers.
Before Magistrate Nurzihan Abdul Rehman, nine local men were fined RM3,500 each after pleading guilty when the charges were read out to them collectively.
They were Liew Ming Hui, 23; Chong Yong Xuan, 25; Gan Kai Lin, 20; Gan Wei Xiang, 23; Myles Tan Yi, 21; Eldrick Tan Chin Lim, 24; Tan Hong Wei, 23; Dennis Chong Wen Wei, 28; and Chuah Kian Wei, 21.
The nine, who are employed full-time, subsequently paid the fines.
In a separate proceeding before Magistrate Atifah Hazimah Wahab, a local man and five Chinese nationals were fined RM4,200 each after pleading guilty.
They were Yau Chin Lin, 33; Dong Ningning, 34; Chen Haihui, 40; Wang Mengnan, 34; Li Xing, 28; and Sun Qixin, 30.
Each was also ordered to serve six months in prison in default of payment, but all six paid the fines.
According to the charge sheets, the accused conspired to commit fraud involving non-existent job offers mainly targeting US citizens.
The offences were committed at two apartment units in East Ledang, Nusajaya, Iskandar Puteri, at 2.40pm and 5.30pm on September 25.
The charges were framed under Section 120B(2) of the Penal Code, read together with Section 417 of the same Code, which provides for up to six months’ imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutors Nor Deana Aqilah Aliman and Sarah Siti Aisyah Mustapha Kamal prosecuted, while the accused were represented by counsel Gan Chee Cheng and Chuah Shyue Chien.

Title: Sarawak police to enlist Interpol over Kuching convenience store attacks
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 30 — Police will seek assistance from international law enforcement agencies, including Interpol, to track several individuals believed to have fled the country in connection with attacks on convenience stores in several parts of Sarawak recently.
Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, who is also the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Management Department director, said three individuals had been arrested so far, while about 10 others had been identified as being linked to the group.
“We have identified about 10 individuals so far, and there may be more from this group. Some have been identified as having fled the country,” he told reporters after attending the Sarawak Police Contingent’s monthly assembly at the state’s Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
He said investigations found that the incidents were believed to stem from a business dispute, including the sale of top-ups allegedly used for online gambling activities.
Mohamad Zainal said police had also identified the misuse of business licences by some convenience stores involved in selling the top-ups and would write to the local authorities (PBT) for further action.
On Sept 21, Mohamad Zainal said police were hunting suspects linked to attacks on convenience stores in Kuching and Sri Aman on Sept 20, in which objects believed to contain explosive or flammable materials were thrown into the premises.
Police received two reports of the incidents, which had a similar modus operandi.
Meanwhile, Mohamad Zainal said police were close to completing their investigation into the Air Medical Services (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, although the cause had yet to be determined.
He said investigations so far had found no indication of sabotage.
“We believe the incident may have been caused by technical problems, but this will depend on the investigation by the Air Accident Investigation Bureau (BSKU), which will announce its findings,” he added. — Bernama
